rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam narrative is retold to alert his descendants to Satan’s snares and to add knowledge after the command to seek increase in knowledge.
rows.anchor: فكان في ذلك مزيد علم له عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The covenant given to Adam means a bequest or admonition.
rows.anchor: والعهد عند الجمهور الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted complement after before most likely means the people warned in the Qur’an, who broke God’s covenant and abandoned faith.
rows.anchor: تقديره من قبل هؤلاء الذين صرف لهم من الوعيد في القرآن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan understands before to mean before the Messenger and the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: من قبل الرسول والقرآن

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another interpretation dates the event to before Adam ate from the tree.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من قبل أن يأكل من الشجرة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reads Adam’s precedent as an example of how the Meccan unbelievers reject signs, disobey messengers, and follow Satan.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: المعنى أن يعرض يا محمد هؤلاء الكفرة عن آياتي ويخالفوا رسلي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects making Adam a model for deniers because Adam sinned through interpretation; he instead allows an independent story or a warning parallel to Muhammad’s instruction not to hasten the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا ضعيف وذلك أن كون آدم مثالا للكفار الجاحدين بالله ليس بشيء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God warned Adam before humanity existed, and his failure to heed the threat establishes a pattern later followed by his descendants.
rows.anchor: لقد أمرنا أباهم آدم ووصيناه أن لا يقرب الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of Adam’s forgetting is that he left the command to guard against the tree and eat its fruit; al-Zamakhshari also allows literal forgetfulness from weak resolve, while Ibn Atiyya excludes absent-mindedness because it would not merit punishment.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن النسيان هنا الترك إن ترك ما وصي به من الاحتراس عن الشجرة

rows.speaker: اليماني والأعمش
rows.claim: They read the verb in a passive form, meaning Satan caused Adam to forget; resolve means firm determination and persistence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليماني والأعمش فنسي بضم النون وتشديد السين أي نساه الشيطان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that Adam lacked firm resolve to persist in abstaining from the tree; finding resolve can mean knowing it or being granted it.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أي على ترك الأكل وأن يتصلب في ذلك تصلبا

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Other explanations say Adam lacked resolve to sin, preserved the command, showed patience against eating, or lacked resolve in careful reasoning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حفظا لما أمر به. وقيل: صبرا عن أكل الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about Iblis refusing is an independent sentence explaining that his noncompliance came from deliberate refusal.
rows.anchor: وأبى جملة مستأنفة مبينة أن امتناعه من السجود إنما كان عن إباء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent omitted object of Iblis’s refusal is prostration, explicitly named in another verse.
rows.anchor: والظاهر حذف متعلق أبى وأنه يقدر هنا ما صرح به في الآية الأخرى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the refusal as a response to an implied question and leaves its object unstated: Iblis displayed resistance and hesitation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري أبى جملة مستأنفة كأنه جواب قائل قال: لم لم يسجد؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Adam and his wife aware of Iblis’s enmity so they could beware, though caution cannot avert destiny.
rows.anchor: عرف تعالى آدم عداوة إبليس له ولزوجته ليحذراه فلن يغني الحذر عن القدر

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: One account attributes Iblis’s hostility to envy when he saw God’s favors upon Adam.
rows.anchor: أن إبليس كان حسودا فلما رأى آثار نعم الله على آدم حسده وعاداه

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another account explains the enmity by the contrast between Iblis’s origin in fire and Adam’s in water and earth.
rows.anchor: العداوة حصلت من تنافي أصليهما إذ إبليس من النار وآدم من الماء والتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against being expelled means Adam and Eve must not obey Satan’s temptation; Satan is credited with the expulsion because his whispering caused their act, though God effected it.
rows.anchor: وأسند الإخراج إليه وإن كان المخرج هو الله تعالى لما كان بوسوسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb meaning you will suffer may be subjunctive after the prohibition or indicative as a separate prediction; it is singular because Adam is addressed and his household’s hardship follows his.
rows.anchor: فتشقى يحتمل أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار أن في جواب النهي، وأن يكون مرفوعا

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: Suffering may mean the toil of earning food, which primarily falls on the man.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالشقاء التعب في طلب القوت وذلك راجع إلى الرجل

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr reports that Adam was given a red ox to plow, so he ate by the labor and sweat of his hand.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن جبير: أهبط له ثور أحمر يحرث عليه فيأكل بكد يمينه

rows.speaker: شيبة ونافع وحفص وابن سعدان
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the hamza in and you will not thirst with kasra, coordinating it with the preceding phrase about Adam’s provision.
rows.anchor: وقرأ شيبة ونافع وحفص وابن سعدان وأنك لا تظمؤا بكسر همزة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority open the hamza, coordinating the clause with the verbal noun meaning that hunger and thirst are absent; coordination permits what direct use of the particle would not.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بفتحها فالكسر عطف على أن لك، والفتح عطف على المصدر المنسبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food, drink, clothing, and shelter are named as sufficient human necessities, while Paradise has far greater pleasures and is free of death, illness, grief, fear, and other burdens.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الشبع والري والكسوة والسكن هي الأمور التي هي ضرورية للإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four negative states name hunger, nakedness, thirst, and exposure to the sun so that Adam would hear the forms of misery and avoid their cause.
rows.anchor: وذكرت هذه الأربعة بلفظ النفي لإثبات أضدادها وهو الشبع والري والكسوة والسكن

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says conventional pairing would match hunger with thirst and nakedness with sun exposure, since nakedness brings cold while sunlight brings heat; Arabic poetry often pairs related things.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وكان عرف الكلام أن يكون الجوع مع الظمأ والعري مع الضحاء

rows.speaker: بعض الأدباء
rows.claim: Some literary critics argue that al-Imru al-Qays’s lines deliberately pair riding horses for pleasure with intimacy, matching activities by their purpose.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب بعض الأدباء إلى أن بيتي امرئ القيس كافطاني للنسب

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: One explanation imagines Adam asking whether Paradise would provide food, clothing, drink, and shade, with the answer matching each concern.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا الجواب على قدر السؤال لما أمر الله آدم بسكنى الجنة

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: A figurative pairing makes hunger and nakedness forms of emptiness inside and outside, and thirst and sun exposure forms of burning inside and outside.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي مقابلة معنوية، فالجوع خلو الباطن، والتعري خلو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lines of al-Imru al-Qays pair riding for pleasure with intimacy, and raiding with urging a horse to charge, answering critics of al-Mutanabbi’s battle imagery.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جمع امرؤ القيس في بيتيه بين ركوب الخيل للذة والنزهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for Satan’s whispering is used with إلى here but with ل in al-Aʿrāf: إلى means conveying the whisper to Adam, while ل may mean for his sake.
rows.anchor: وتعدى وسوس هنا بإلى وفي الأعراف باللام، فالتعدي بإلى معناه أنهى الوسوسة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan called Adam by name to secure his attention, then offered advice through a question, a tactful form that encourages acceptance.
rows.anchor: ولما وسوس إليه ناداه باسمه ليكون أقبل عليه وأمكن للاستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan tempted Adam with the same promise of lasting comfort that God had already used to encourage him to remain in Paradise.
rows.anchor: فجاءه إبليس من الجهة التي رغبه الله فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Aʿrāf Satan first claims God prohibited the tree; here he first offers immortality, then names the prohibition after seeing Adam incline toward him.
rows.anchor: والجمع بينهما أن قوله هل أدلك يكون سابقا على قوله ما نهاكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question form of Satan’s offer sounds like considerate counsel, comparable to Moses’s invitation to purification.
rows.anchor: كقول موسى هل لك إلى أن تزكى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, citing Ibn Abbas, says Adam violated the divine command; his act was disobedience and therefore the opposite of right guidance.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري عن ابن عباس: لا شبهة في أن آدم صلوات الله عليه لم يمتثل

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says one may report Adam’s disobedience only while quoting revelation, not independently, given Adam’s exalted status as the first forefather and prophet whom God chose and forgave.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي: لا يجوز لأحدنا اليوم أن يخبر بذلك عنه

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi extends the rule to divine attributes: descriptions such as hand or descent should not be initiated outside scripture; he cites Malik’s rebuke of anthropomorphic gestures.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي: وإذا كان هذا في المخلوق لا يجوز والإخبار عن صفات الله كاليد والرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s choosing Adam means selecting and drawing him near; turning to him means accepting his repentance; guidance may mean prophethood, knowledge of repentance, or return to remorse.
rows.anchor: ثم اجتباه أي اصطفاه وقربه وتاب عليه أي قبل توبته وهدى أي هداه للنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual command to descend addresses Adam and Eve together; all together describes their joint descent, not the presence of Satan and the serpent.
rows.anchor: ولا يدل قوله جميعا أن إبليس والحية يهبطان معهما لأن جميعا حال من ضمير الاثنين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Satan and the serpent descend with Adam and Eve and that hostility between them and their descendants continues to the end of time.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ثم أخبرهما بقوله جميعا أن إبليس والحية مهبطان معهما

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: One reading identifies the hostile groups as Iblis and his descendants opposed to Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: قيل: يريد إبليس وبنيه وآدم وبنيه

rows.speaker: قول ثان
rows.claim: Another reading takes the hostility as between Adam and his descendants, owing to divergent religions and opinions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد آدم وذريته، فالعداوة واقعة بينهم والبغضاء لاختلاف الأديان

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the dual address refers to Adam and Satan as two species, each encompassing many descendants, which explains the later plural address.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم الأصبهاني: الخطاب لآدم عليه السلام ولكونهما جنسين صح قوله اهبطا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Adam and Eve stand for humanity because all people descend from them, explaining why they are addressed with a plural verb.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لما كان آدم وحواء عليهما السلام أصلي البشر والسببين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised guidance means God’s law; following the Qur’an protects from worldly error and misery in the afterlife, while one report specifies protection from bad reckoning.
rows.anchor: وهدى شريعة الله. وعن ابن عباس ضمن الله لمن اتبع القرآن أن لا يضل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi defines guidance as following evidence through both inference and practice; it guarantees no afterlife error or misery because God guides the follower to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: وهذه الآية تدل على أن المراد بالهدى الذي ذكره الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another view places the promise in this world; the response says it excludes religious error and hardship caused by religion, not troubles from other causes.
rows.anchor: وقيل فلا يضل ولا يشقى في الدنيا. فإن قيل: المنعم بهدى الله قد يلحقه الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from God’s reminder, meaning the Qur’an or other revealed books, brings a constricted, difficult life; ḍank is an invariant adjective for hardship.
rows.anchor: والذكر يقع على القرآن وعلى سائر الكتب الإلهية. وضنك: مصدر يوصف به المذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line by Antara illustrates a constricted dwelling as a source of hardship.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول عنترة: إن المنية لو تمثل مثلت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi and refers to the grave squeezing the ribs.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: نزلت هذه الآية في الأسود بن عبد الأسد المخزومي

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والكلبي
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and al-Kalbi interpret the constricted life as the narrow life of Hell, where food and drink are torment and inhabitants neither die nor live.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة والكلبي: هو الضيق في الآخرة في جهنم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says a disbeliever’s life is constricted because he lacks certainty about reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: المعيشة الضنك معيشة الكافر لأنه غير موقن بالثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets the hardship as loss of contentment, leaving a person perpetually unsatisfied.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: يسلب القناعة حتى لا يشبع

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والسدي
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri and al-Suddi identify it as grave punishment; Abu Hurayra transmits this interpretation from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري والسدي: هو عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari places the hardship in worldly life: even a wealthy unbeliever is distressed by greed, ambition, worldly troubles, and lack of ease.
rows.anchor: وقال الجوهري: المعيشة الضنك في الدنيا، والمعنى أن الكافر وإن كان متسع الحال والمال

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says the constricted livelihood comes from eating unlawful food.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة ضنكا بأكل الحرام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says faith brings submission, contentment, trust, and generous spending, while unbelief brings greed and stinginess; he links this to the promise of a good life.
rows.anchor: فصاحبه ينفق ما رزقه بسماح وسهولة فيعيش عيشا طيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence about being gathered blind and the greater, lasting punishment supports taking the constricted life as a punishment before the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ويستدل على أن المعيشة الضنك قبل يوم القيامة ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads ḍankī with feminine alif, no tanwin, and imāla; the majority read ḍankan with tanwin and an inflected final vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ضنكي بألف التأنيث ولا تنوين وبالإمالة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read we shall gather with nūn; a group including Aban reads the rāʾ still, either as lightening or as jussive coordination with the conditional response, while another group reads the verb with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ونحشره بالنون، وفرقة منهم أبان بن تغلب بسكون الراء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the gathering as blind in eyesight, as in another verse; Ibn Atiyya argues that blindness of insight would not be newly felt by unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله أعمى المراد به عمى البصر كما قال ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل وأبو صالح
rows.claim: These interpreters, with a report also from Ibn Abbas, say the person is blind to any argument that could guide him.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل وأبو صالح وروي عن ابن عباس: أعمى عن حجته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person is first gathered with sight, then becomes blind upon reaching the gathering place.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس يحشر بصيرا ثم إذا استوى إلى المحشر أعمى

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Other explanations say he is helpless to escape punishment, blind to everything but Hell, or unable to find his way; al-Jubbaʾi adopts the last view.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعمى عن الحيلة في دفع العذاب عن نفسه كالأعمى

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn ʿArafa says every blameworthy blindness in scripture means blindness of the heart, citing the verse that hearts rather than eyes become blind.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن عرفة: كل ما ذكره الله عز وجل في كتابه فذمه فإنما يريد عمى القلب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the servant’s question as saying he has no defense, although in worldly life he knew and could argue his case.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معنى لم حشرتني أعمى أي لا حجة لي وقد كنت عالما بحجتي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that God’s signs came clearly but the person ignored and failed to consider them, so he is left in blindness and punishment in return.
rows.anchor: كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting here means abandoning the signs, and being forgotten means being left in punishment rather than suffering absent-mindedness.
rows.anchor: والنسيان هنا بمعنى الترك لا بمعنى الذهول، ومعنى تنسى تترك في العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife punishment is greater than worldly punishment and lasts because it does not end; al-Zamakhshari also compares permanent blindness with temporary hardship.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن عذاب الآخرة أشد أي من عذاب الدنيا لأنه أعظم منه وأبقى

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi reports a view that the interrogative كم is the subject of the verb, which Abū Hayyān rejects because interrogatives cannot be governed by a preceding verb.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: قال بعضهم هي في موضع رفع فاعل يهد وأنكر هذا على قائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here كم is a declarative expression of many, not a question, so it can be governed by the verb.
rows.anchor: وليست كم هنا استفهاما بل هي خبرية

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows God as the implicit subject of yehd, with yehd meaning make known, as in another verse’s use of clarify.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: يهد لهم في فاعله وجهان أحدهما ضمير اسم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن السميفع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ reads they walk in a passive form because walking is created step by step through motions and rests.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع: يمشون بالتشديد مبنيا للمفعول لأن المشي يخلق خطوة بخطوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Quraysh, who traveled through the lands of earlier destroyed peoples on their routes to Syria and saw their ruins.
rows.anchor: وهم الكفار الموبخون يريد قريشا، والعرب يتقلبون في بلاد عاد وثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The walking phrase can describe Quraysh as they tour the ruins, or the destroyed peoples as they lived securely in their homes before sudden destruction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حال من مفعول أهلكنا أي أهلكناهم غارين آمنين متصرفين في مساكنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of earlier peoples provides signs for sound-minded people.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك أي في ذلك التبيين بإهلاك القرون الماضية لآيات لأولي النهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior decree postpones the deniers’ punishment until the Hour; otherwise they would have faced the immediate destruction that struck earlier nations.
rows.anchor: لولا هذه العدة لكان مثل إهلاكنا عادا وثمودا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says God recorded for the angels, scriptures, and Preserved Tablet that Muhammad’s community would not be annihilated like earlier peoples despite rejecting him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: لا شبهة أن الكلمة إخبار الله تعالى ملائكته وكتبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word لزام can be a verbal noun used adjectivally for binding, or an intensive noun meaning an instrument that enforces binding.
rows.anchor: واللزام إما مصدر لازم وصف به وإما فعال بمعنى مفعل

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: The appointed term may mean the unbelievers’ lifespan; the associated punishment then includes the grave and what follows.
rows.anchor: والأجل أجل حياتهم أو أجل إهلاكهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قول ثان
rows.claim: If the term means their worldly destruction, the punishment is their killing at Badr.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني: قتلهم بالسيف يوم بدر

rows.speaker: قول ثالث
rows.claim: If the term means the Day of Resurrection, the punishment is Hell.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثالث: هو عذاب جهنم

rows.speaker: صحيح البخاري
rows.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari identifies the day of Badr as the binding punishment and the great seizure.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري «أن يوم بدر هو اللزام وهو البطشة الكبرى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term appears coordinated with the prior word but is delayed after the conditional clause to preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عطف وأجل مسمى على كلمة وأخر المعطوف عن المعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead coordinates the appointed term with the hidden subject of was, making both immediate taking and a fixed term binding together.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون وأجل معطوفا على الضمير المستكن في كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad to bear Quraysh’s abusive speech and to glorify and praise God, either in words or through declaring Him free of their false claims.
rows.anchor: ثم أمره تعالى بالصبر على ما يقول مشركو قريش، وهم الذين عاد الضمير عليهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads the command as glorifying and exalting God, rather than prescribing specific wording.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: لا يبعد حمله على التنزيه والإجلال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi prefers the glorification reading because it follows the command to endure denials and counteracts their claims of disbelief and association.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله الرازي: وهذا القول أقرب إلى الظاهر وإلى ما تقدم ذكره

rows.speaker: قول في التفسير
rows.claim: A prayer interpretation maps the times to dawn, afternoon, evening, nightfall, and midday prayers.
rows.anchor: فقبل طلوع الشمس صلاة الصبح وقبل غروبها صلاة العصر ومن آناء الليل المغرب والعتمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows the wording to mean saying subhan Allah and praise after dawn prayer through the forenoon prayer and before sunset.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويحتمل اللفظ أن يراد قول سبحان الله وبحمده

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that whoever glorifies God seventy times at sunset has his sins erased.
rows.anchor: فقد قال عليه السلام: «من سبح عند غروب الشمس سبعين تسبيحة غربت بذنوبه»

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari maps before sunset to noon and afternoon, night portions to nightfall prayer, and day edges to sunset and dawn prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقبل غروبها يعني الظهر والعصر لأنهما واقعتان في النصف الأخير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says night worship is especially meritorious because it allows focus and privacy, and is harder than using the body’s resting time; he links it with other night-worship verses.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أفضل الذكر ما كان بالليل لاجتماع القلب وهدو الرجل والخلو بالرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation compares the plural edges of day to poetic dual forms, despite day having only two edges.
rows.anchor: فقيل: جاء على حد قوله:

rows.speaker: قول ثان
rows.claim: Another takes the plural literally: dawn is one edge, noon and afternoon another, and sunset and nightfall a third.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو على حقيقة الجمع الفجر الطرف الأول

rows.speaker: قول ثالث
rows.claim: Another account counts four edges at sunrise, sunset, solar noon, and the sun’s pause at noon.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النهار له أربعة أطراف عند طلوع الشمس، وعند غروبها، وعند زوال الشمس

rows.speaker: قول رابع
rows.claim: Another says midday prayer straddles the two day edges while sunset marks a third edge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الظهر في آخر طرف النهار الأول، وأول طرف النهار الآخر

rows.speaker: قول خامس
rows.claim: Other readings explain the plural by treating day as a recurring genus or by using edges to mean hours.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يجعل النهار للجنس فلكل يوم طرف فيتكرر بتكرره. وقيل: المراد بالأطراف الساعات

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the word for edges in the accusative, coordinating it with night portions; Hasan and Isa ibn Umar read it in the genitive, coordinating it with night portions grammatically.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وأطراف بنصب الفاء وهو معطوف على ومن آناء الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope of being pleased means receiving a reward that one will see, expressed as hope rather than certainty; another view makes divine hope necessarily fulfilled.
rows.anchor: لعلك ترضى أي تثاب على هذه الأعمال بالثواب الذي تراه

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وأبو بكر وأبان
rows.claim: These readers use a passive form meaning that the Lord will make Muhammad pleased.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وأبو بكر وأبان وعصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After patience and glorification, Muhammad is told not to prolong his gaze at the worldly goods given to unbelievers, which are temporary like a flower.
rows.anchor: ولما أمره تعالى بالصبر وبالتسبيح جاء النهي عن مد البصر إلى ما متع به الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning includes their wealth, children, homes, transport, clothing, and food; the address to the Prophet applies to his community, since he was least attached to worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: ولا تعجب يا محمد مما متعناهم به من مال وبنين ومنازل ومراكب وملابس

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying describes the world and its contents as cursed except what is sought for God’s sake.
rows.anchor: وهو القائل في الدنيا «ملعونة ملعون ما فيها إلا ما أريد به وجه الله»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stretching one’s gaze is stronger than simply looking, since it implies prolonged admiration; a brief involuntary glance is excused.
rows.anchor: ولا تمدن أبلغ من لا تنظر لأن مد البصر يقتضي الإدامة والاستحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious avert their eyes from the luxury of tyrants and immoral people because the display is meant to attract spectators and their attention encourages its owners.
rows.anchor: فالناظر إليها محصل لغرضهم وكالمغري لهم على اتخاذها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwājan is parsed as a direct object, meaning groups of unbelievers, with منهم as its modifier; al-Zamakhshari offers an alternative circumstantial parsing.
rows.anchor: وانتصب أزواجا على أنه مفعول به، والمعنى أصنافا من الكفرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows azwājan to be a circumstantial accusative, while taking منهم as the object of bestowed, meaning some groups of people.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن ينتصب أزواجا عن الحال من ضمير به

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: The word flower has several proposed syntactic roles, including blame, a second object, apposition, predicate, or circumstantial accusative; Makkī prefers the final analysis, while apposition to the pronoun is rejected for separating the verb from its complement.
rows.anchor: وزَهرة منصوب على الذم أو مفعول ثان لمتعنا على تضمينه معنى أعطينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good outcome, or praiseworthy end, belongs to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: والعاقبة أي الحميدة أو حسن العاقبة لأهل التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers habitually demand a sign of their own choosing and dismiss the signs already shown; the Qur’an answers that earlier scriptures had foretold it and that it is the enduring, greatest miracle.
rows.anchor: هذه عادتهم في اقتراح الآيات كأنهم جعلوا ما ظهر من الآيات ليس بآيات

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص
rows.claim: These readers use the feminine verb form matching the word sign; other readers use masculine agreement because the feminine noun is separated from the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص تأتهم بالتاء على لفظ بينة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read proof in construct with what is in the earlier pages; a group reads it indefinite with tanwin and takes what as an appositive, with further case variants also reported.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بإضافة بينة إلى ما وفرقة منهم أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو بالتنوين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads pages with a still ḥāʾ rather than the majority’s rounded vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور في الصحف بضم الحاء، وفرقة منهم ابن عباس بإسكانها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the pronoun in before it to refer to the proof; the apparent reading instead refers to the Messenger, based on the following mention of sending one.
rows.anchor: والضمير في ضمن قبله يعود على البينة لأنها في معنى البرهان

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: One explanation places humiliation in this life and disgrace in the afterlife; another treats humiliation and disgrace as near synonyms.
rows.anchor: وقيل نذل في الدنيا ونخزى في الآخرة. وقيل: الذل الهوان والخزي الافتضاح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومحمد بن الحنفية وزيد بن علي والحسن
rows.claim: These readers use passive forms for we shall be humiliated and disgraced, unlike the majority’s active forms.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس ومحمد بن الحنفية وزيد بن علي والحسن في رواية عباد

none: Qur’anic text only; no commentary or other source claims.

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub glosses being distracted as becoming occupied with something else.
rows.anchor: ذهل عن الشيء ذهولا: اشتغل عنه قاله قطرب

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another lexicographer explains distraction as inattentiveness caused by a sudden burden such as worry or pain; another explanation is bewilderment.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: غفل لطريان شاغل من أهم أو وجع أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A morsel is a small piece of flesh about the size one can chew; formed means smoothed and complete without defect.
rows.anchor: المضغة: اللحمة الصغيرة قدر ما يمضغ. المخلقة: المسواة الملساء لا نقص ولا عيب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Child can name the period from birth to puberty, a young animal, or an adjective for any gender or number; related forms also describe having a child or gentleness.
rows.anchor: الطفل: يقال من وقت انفصال الولد إلى البلوغ، ويقال لولد الوحشية طفل

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says child is a verbal noun like satisfaction or justice and can refer to one or many.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: هو اسم يستعمل مصدرا كالرضا والعدل يقع على الواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: The verb for earth becoming barren can mean drying and falling into ruin; the same root can describe a worn garment.
rows.anchor: همدت الأرض: يبست ودرست، والثوب بلي

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s verse uses the word for barren and worn to describe clothing.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعشى: قالت قتيلة ما لجسمك شاحبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bihīj means beautiful and pleasing to the eye, with related forms meaning beauty or delight.
rows.anchor: فلان ذو بهجة أي حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for side means a flank; a man’s two sides are his right and left, and a cloak is named for hanging over the side.
rows.anchor: العطف: الجانب، وعطفا الرجل يمينه وشماله

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: The Magians are variously described as worshipping fire, sun, and moon, or fire alone; other reports describe ascetics or a mixed community.
rows.anchor: المجوس: قوم يعبدون النار والشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Other descriptions say the Magians borrowed elements from Christians and Jews or taught that the world has two principles, light and darkness; one etymology links their name to impurities.
rows.anchor: وهم القائلون العالم أصلان نور وظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word deep can also be pronounced with ghayn; al-Layth records the Tamim forms for deep.
rows.anchor: ويقال: عميق بالغين. وقال الليث: يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ritual grime means dirt or filth, also used as a rebuke to someone appearing dirty.
rows.anchor: التفث: أصله الوسخ والقذر، يقال لمن يستقذر

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammakh’s verse uses the petitioner sense of a person who comes seeking a favor.
rows.anchor: قال الشماخ: مفاقرة أعف من القنوع

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Al-Layth says Tamim uses both ʿamīq and maʿīq and related forms for great depth or the edges of a desert; poetry illustrates the latter.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: يقال عميق ومعيق لتميم، وأعمقت البئر

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: The word for ritual grime means dirt; Qutrub says a traveler becomes especially dirty on a journey, while another explanation traces it to fingernail grime.
rows.anchor: وعن قطرب: تفث الرجل كثر وسخه في سفره

rows.speaker: أبو محمد البصري
rows.claim: Abu Muhammad al-Basri derives the term from dirt under fingernails, with a sound change from fāʾ to thāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو محمد البصري: التفث من التف وهو وسخ الأظفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saḥīq means distant; a thing that falls has collapsed, and the sun’s setting is also expressed with the same root.
rows.anchor: السحيق: البعيد. وجب الشيء سقط، ووجبت الشمس جبة

rows.speaker: أوس بن حجر
rows.claim: Aws ibn Hajar’s verse uses the root for the setting sun.
rows.anchor: قال أوس بن حجر: ألم يكسف الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One form of qāniʿ means a petitioner, while another means someone content with little and self-sufficient; al-Shammakh’s verse shows the petitioner sense.
rows.anchor: القانع: السائل، قنع قنوعا سأل وقنع قناعة تعفف

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Shammar defines an idol as any statue made from common materials and notes that the word can refer to a cross; Arabs set such figures up for worship.
rows.anchor: قال شمر كل تمثال من خشب أو حجارة أو ذهب أو فضة أو نحاس

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim to remove the cross from his neck, calling it an idol.
rows.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعدي بن حاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for idol comes from setting something firmly in place; the related adjective means settled and fixed, and poetry uses it for steadfastness in a covenant.
rows.anchor: واشتقاقه من وثن الشيء أقامه في مكانه وثبت، والواثن المقيم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says sacrificial camels is a plural of sacrificial animal, named for becoming large and fat.
rows.anchor: البدن: جمع بدنة كثمر جمع ثمرة قاله الزجاج، سميت بذلك

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says a sacrificial animal can be a camel or cow but not a sheep; other opinions restrict it to camels or include marked camels and cows.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: البدنة بالهاء تقع على الناقة والبقرة والبعير مما يجوز في الهدي

rows.speaker: عطاء وغيره
rows.claim: Ata and others restrict the sacrificial animal to a marked camel or cow; another view treats the word as a generic for large, fat camels and cattle.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما أشعر من ناقة أو بقرة قاله عطاء وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says a person called muʿtar comes seeking a favor without asking directly; the word also has forms meaning to visit for a kindness.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: عره واعتره وعراه واعتراه أتاه طالبا لمعروفه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say the surah is Meccan except the passage about the two disputing parties through three verses; another report from Ibn Abbas extends the exception by one verse.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد، وعن ابن عباس أيضا إنهن أربع آيات إلى قوله عذاب الحريق

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the surah is Medinan.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هي مدنية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada places the Medinan portion beginning with the statement about messengers and ending at the threat of humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: إلا من قوله وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the surah contains both Meccan and Medinan passages.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: منها مكي ومنها مدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening follows the preceding discussion of the blessed and wretched and the terror of Judgment; because Meccan deniers rejected resurrection while punishment was delayed, this surah warns them through the quake, the fate of its deniers, human development, and the earth reviving after barrenness.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه السورة تحذيرا لهم وتخويفا لما انطوت عليه من ذكر زلزلة الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to people is apparently universal, though another reading narrows it to Meccans; fearing their Lord means fearing His punishment.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله يا أيها الناس عام. وقيل: المراد أهل مكة

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: The earthquake is placed at the first blast; other accounts place it at the second blast or at the command to Adam to bring forth the Fire’s destined group.
rows.anchor: والزلزلة الحركة المزعجة وهي عند النفخة الأولى. وقيل: عند الثانية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the earthquake occurs on the Day of Resurrection; Alqama and al-Shaʿbi place it at the sun’s rising from the west, a sign of the Hour.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن: يوم القيامة. وعن علقمة والشعبي: عند طلوح الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive phrase earthquake of the Hour can treat the Hour as cause or as the object affected; the omitted object earth is inferred from another verse, and on either analysis the earthquake is real.
rows.anchor: والمصدر مضاف للفاعل فالمفعول المحذوف وهو الأرض

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the greatest earthquake accompanies the onset of the Hour.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: أشد الزلزال ما يكون مع قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the earthquake figuratively as the Hour’s greatest terrors rather than a physical shaking.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الزلزلة استعارة، والمراد أشد الساعة وأهوال يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the not-yet-occurring earthquake a thing is valid because its occurrence is certain; those who reject this usage explain that it is named as a thing because it will exist.
rows.anchor: وشيء هنا يدل على إطلاقه على المعدوم لأن الزلزلة لم تقع بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terrifying details are set before readers so they can imagine them and be moved to piety, the only protection from those trials.
rows.anchor: لينظروا إلى تلك الصفة ببصائرهم ويتصوروها بعقولهم ليكون ذلك حاملا على تقواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the two verses were revealed at night during the Banu al-Mustaliq expedition; after the Prophet recited them, many companions wept and spent the next morning grieving or reflecting.
rows.anchor: وروي أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا ليلا في غزوة بني المصطلق فقرأهما رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in you see it apparently refers to the earthquake, which suits literal nursing and childbirth in this world; Hasan says the nursing woman abandons her child and the pregnant woman gives birth prematurely.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير المنصوب في ترونها عائدا على الزلزلة لأنها المحدث عنها

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group takes the pronoun as the Hour, using nursing and childbirth as images for the overwhelming terror of that day.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الضمير يعود على الساعة فيكون الذهول والوضع عبارة عن شدة الهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine participle means a woman actively nursing, rather than one who merely has a nursing role; a poem uses the active form for a woman nursing another’s child.
rows.anchor: وجاء لفظ مرضعة دون مرضع لأنه أريد به الفعل لا النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority place the earthquake at the end of the world, followed by the sun rising from the west.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا آخر الزمان ويتبعها طلوع الشمس من مغربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun in about what she nursed has an omitted object, supported by the concrete object in the next phrase; another view makes it a verbal noun meaning nursing.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ما في قوله عما أرضعت بمعنى الذي، والعائد محذوف أي أرضعته

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari distinguishes a woman actively breastfeeding from one generally charged with nursing, and says the verse depicts the earthquake striking while the baby is latched on.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: المرضعة هي التي في حال الإرضاع تلقم ثديها الصبي

rows.speaker: بعض نحاة الكوفة
rows.claim: Some Kufan grammarians reserve the form ending in tāʾ for a mother and the form without it for a hired nurse, but a poetic example refutes the restriction.
rows.anchor: وخص بعض نحاة الكوفة أم الصبي بمرضعة والمستأجرة بمرضع وهذا باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that exclusively feminine descriptions need no tāʾ is contradicted by common forms such as nursing, menstruating, and divorced.
rows.anchor: وقول الكوفيين إن الوصف الذي يختص بالمؤنث لا يحتاج فيه إلى التاء لأنها إنما جيء بها للفرق

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verb as active with every nursing woman as its nominative subject; Ibn Abi Abla and al-Yamani read it in a passive pattern with the earthquake or Hour as subject and each woman in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تذهل كل بفتح التاء والهاء ورفع كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for burden can mean a load in the womb or fruit carried on a tree.
rows.anchor: والحمل بالفتح ما كان في بطن أو على رأس شجرة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read you see as direct address; other readers use passive forms with the earthquake or Hour as subject, and the people are described as appearing drunk by simile rather than from wine.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وترى بالتاء مفتوحة خطاب المفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading of the people makes see govern three objects; people are likened to the drunk through confusion and disordered reason, while the text denies literal drunkenness.
rows.anchor: أثبت أنهم سكارى على طريق التشبيه ثم نفى عنهم الحقيقة وهي السكر من الخمر

rows.speaker: عبد الله وأصحابه وحذيفة
rows.claim: The reading sukrā is also attributed to Abdullah, his companions, and Hudhayfa.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة عبد الله وأصحابه وحذيفة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says some use sukrā like marḍā for paired states entering a person, and compares it with rūbā for those made sleepy by fermented milk.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه: وقوم يقولون سكرى جعلوه مثل مرضى

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says sukrā could be the plural of sakr, since Sibawayh attests sakr as a word meaning drunk.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: ويصح أن يكون جمع سكر كزمنى وزمن

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعرج وأبو زرعة وابن جبير والأعمش
rows.claim: These readers pronounce sukrā with ḍamma on the sīn; Abu al-Fath calls it a singular noun like good tidings, while al-Zamakhshari calls it unusual.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعرج وأبو زرعة وابن جبير والأعمش سكرى بضم السين

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
rows.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi explains the feminine singular adjective by treating the human collective as a single feminine entity.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الفضل الرازي: فعلى بضم الفاء من صفة الواحدة من الإناث

rows.speaker: أبو زرعة
rows.claim: Abu Zurʿa also transmits a layered variant combining an open sīn with a form whose sīn is rounded.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي زرعة أيضا سكرى بفتح السين بسكرى بضمها

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr also transmits sukrā without the long vowel alongside the form with the long vowel.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن جبير أيضا سكرى بالفتح من غير ألف بسكارى بالضم والألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from plural address to singular makes each person see all others in the terror-induced state of people whose reason is impaired by intoxication.
rows.anchor: ثم قال وترى على خطاب الواحد لأن الرؤية معلقة بكون الناس على حال السكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast says that the visible confusion is mild compared with God’s severe punishment; لكن links opposing conditions.
rows.anchor: وكأنه قيل: وهذه أحوال هينة ولكن عذاب الله شديد

rows.speaker: قول أول
rows.claim: Some say the person arguing about God without knowledge was Abu Jahl; others name Ubayy ibn Khalaf and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, or al-Nadr alone.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في أبي جهل. وقيل: في أبي بن خلف والنضر بن الحارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also applies generally to anyone arguing without knowledge, guidance, or proof about what God may or may not do; the rebellious satan is apparently a jinn, though human devils are possible.
rows.anchor: والآية في كل من تعاطى الجدال فيما يجوز على الله وما لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the terrors of Judgment, the passage turns to those heedless of requital and denying it.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى أهوال يوم القيامة ذكر من غفل عن الجزاء في ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads the verb for following with a light consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ويتبع خفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns apparently refer to the person who argues: that person follows the devil and whoever allies with him is led astray; the pronoun may instead mean the matter or disposition of the follower.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في عليه عائد على من لأنه المحدث عنه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes the pronoun in against him to refer to the rebellious devil.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في عليه عائد على كل شيطان مريد قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya’s preferred analysis assigns the first pronoun to Satan and the second to the person who follows him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويظهر لي أن الضمير في أنه الأولى للشيطان والثانية لمن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the decree was inscribed against the follower because his state plainly shows that he will be led astray.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والكتبة عليه مثل أي إنما كتب إضلال من يتولاه عليه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the decree in a passive form and open both particles; the two clauses’ coordination is grammatically criticized because it leaves the conditional or relative clause without its required completion.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أنه بفتح الهمزة في موضع المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: الأعمش والجعفي عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: These readers pronounce both particles with kasra; Ibn Atiyya attributes the reading to Abu Amr more broadly, but the author says that attribution is not well known.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والجعفي عن أبي عمرو أنه فإنه بكسر الهمزتين

rows.speaker: قراءة أخرى
rows.claim: An alternate reading makes the verb wrote active, with God as its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرىء كتب مبنيا للفاعل أي كتب الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers an implied saying verb or a passive subject analysis for the clause after the decree; Abū Hayyān rejects both in Basran grammar.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو عن تقدير قيل أو على المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran grammarians do not allow a clause as the passive subject, and they do not open a following particle after a verb meaning say unless the saying verb is explicit.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يجوز عند البصريين لأن الفاعل عندهم لا يكون جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two clear arguments answer doubts about resurrection: human development through successive stages and the earth’s observable movement from barrenness to life; reason establishes possibility and revelation confirms its occurrence.
rows.anchor: ذكر دليلين واضحين على ذلك أحدهما في نفس الإنسان وابتداء خلقه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads resurrection with fatḥa on the middle consonant, a dialect form; Kufans analogize such vowel reduction around gutturals while Basrans treat attested cases as separate dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن من البعث بفتح العين وهي لغة فيه كالحلب والطرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity comes from soil through Adam or through reproductive foods ultimately derived from land and water; the seed is semen, though al-Naqqash says it was Adam’s seed.
rows.anchor: من تراب أي أصلكم آدم وسلط الفعل عليهم من حيث هم من ذريته

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash interprets the seed in this sequence as Adam’s own seed.
rows.anchor: والنطفة المني. وقيل نطفة آدم قاله النقاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clot is a piece of congealed blood; unformed means incomplete or unsmoothed, explaining variation in stature and completeness.
rows.anchor: والعلقة قطعة الدم الجامدة ومعنى وغير مخلقة أي ليست كاملة ولا ملساء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبو العالية
rows.claim: These authorities say an unformed embryo is one that is miscarried.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد غير مخلقة هي التي تستسقط وقاله قتادة والشعبي وأبو العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb form intensifies the idea of creation because the human body contains many distinct organs, each fashioned with its own form.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان فيه أعضاء متباينة وكل واحد منها مختص بخلق حسن تضعيف الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase leads him is ironic: it means driving him toward the blazing punishment under the guise of guidance.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ويهديه ويسوقه وعبر بلفظ الهداية على سبيل التهكم

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads formed and unformed as accusatives describing the preceding indefinite noun, a rare but analogically acceptable construction according to Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة مخلقة بالنصب وغير بالنصب أيضا نصبا على الحال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the stages show that the one who first created humans from unrelated soil and water can recreate them, which is even easier by analogy; the acts reveal knowledge and power beyond human grasp.
rows.anchor: ولنبين لكم بهذا التدريج قدرتنا وإن من قدر على خلق البشر من تراب أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause to clarify is connected to created you; Ibn Atiyya instead takes it as an aside explaining resurrection, while al-Kirmani says it clarifies guidance and error.
rows.anchor: ولنبين متعلق بخلقناكم. وقيل لنبين لكم أمر البعث. قال ابن عطية:

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another interpretation says formation is a choice of the choosing agent, which explains why some embryos remain unformed.
rows.anchor: وقيل لنبين لكم أن التخليق هو اختيار من الفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads the clause with a third-person verb, clarifying the process for you.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ليبين لكم ويقر بالياء

rows.speaker: يعقوب وعاصم في رواية
rows.claim: Yaqub and one transmission from Asim read we settle in the wombs in the accusative, coordinating it with to clarify.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وعاصم في رواية ونقر بالنصب عطفا على لنبين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the nominative reading as a statement that God keeps in the womb whoever He chooses until birth; the accusative makes keeping another purpose so the children may be born, grow, and reach responsibility.
rows.anchor: والقراءة بالنصب تعليل معطوف على تعليل والمعنى خلقناكم مدرجين هذا التدريج لغرضين

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub also reads we settle with the verb form meaning pour out water; other named readers vary between accusative and nominative forms for settle and bring you out.
rows.anchor: وعن يعقوب ونقر بفتح النون وضم القاف والراء من قر الماء صبه

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads what We will with kasra on the nūn; the appointed term varies for each fetus according to whether it miscarries or is carried to completion and live birth.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب ما نشاء بكسر النون والأجل المسمى مختلف فيه بحسب جنين

rows.speaker: المبرد والطبري
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Tabari explain child as a singular verbal noun or generic term, and it is also singular because the sense is each one of you.
rows.anchor: وحد طفلا لأنه مصدر في الأصل قاله المبرد والطبري
